title: Interfaces, channels, and modules
summary: Run work in a goroutine, receive the result from a channel, and reason about module boundaries.

scenario.briefing: A reporting endpoint sums a batch on a worker goroutine. Move the work off the request path and receive the result safely.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Diagnose a realistic mistake and choose the correct repair.

hints: Start an anonymous goroutine with go func().
Send the total into the channel.
Return the value received from the channel.

misconceptions.description: Sending on an unbuffered channel without a receiver.
misconceptions.testDescription: The work runs in a goroutine and returns through a channel.
misconceptions.feedback: The send blocks until another goroutine receives. Receive from the channel in the caller.

misconceptions.description: Writing to a shared variable from several goroutines without synchronization.
misconceptions.feedback: Use channels or a mutex. Unsynchronized shared writes are a data race.

misconceptions.description: Closing a channel instead of receiving from it.
misconceptions.feedback: Closing does not consume the sent value. The function must receive from the channel.

sections.title: Go functions and collections
sections.body: Functions declare parameter and return types: func add(left int, right int) int { return left + right }. A slice such as []int{3, -1, 2} is a view over an array. An interface describes behavior, and a type satisfies it by implementing its methods.

sections.title: Go errors and tools
sections.body: Functions return errors explicitly: value, err := strconv.Atoi(text); if err != nil { ... }. steps.title: Concurrency and modules

statements.label: A Go type satisfies an interface by implementing its methods, without an explicit declaration.
An unbuffered channel send blocks until a receiver is ready.
A goroutine blocks the entire process until it finishes.
Go modules record exact dependency versions for reproducible builds.

steps.explanation: Goroutines run concurrently, and channels synchronize their communication. Interfaces are satisfied implicitly, while modules pin dependencies.
hints: A goroutine does not block the whole process.
